title: Lab 1: FPGA and Board Testing
text:
Simulation
Questa testbenches reported PASS for the decoder, counter, and top-level connections.


Hexadecimal decoder waveform




Questa decoder simulation supplied during testing.


Inputs step from 0 to F; each produces the expected segment pattern. For example, 0 gives 7'h40 and 8 gives 7'h00. Zero bits illuminate segments.



Counter waveform




Questa counter simulation supplied during testing.


With the test maximum set to 3, the count cycles 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0. Rollover toggles blink. Disabling holds both values; reset clears them on the next rising clock edge. Initial red values occur before the first reset clock edge.



Top-level waveform




Questa top-level simulation supplied during testing.


The simulated oscillator period is approximately 20.832 ns. The test checks both LED expressions, decoder connections, reset, enable, and blinking with MAX_COUNT=3. This shortened test verifies connections; it does not measure the hardware’s 2.4 Hz blink rate.

title: Lab 2: Multiplexed Seven-Segment Display
text: Two independently controlled hexadecimal digits were time-multiplexed through one seven-segment decoder. A 4 × 4 keypad scanner drove four open-collector rows and displayed the sensed columns on four LEDs.

title: Lab 2: Multiplexed Seven-Segment Display
text:
AI Prototype

Reflection: # AI Prototype Summary
AI was used to generate an initial HDL structure, testbenches, and wiring plan. The prototype suggested reusing the Lab 1 counter, sharing one seven-segment decoder between both digits, and scanning the keypad rows with a counter. The generated design provided a useful starting point but required corrections to match the active-low display signals, actual FPGA pin assignments, component values, and physical wiring. QuestaSim verified the digital behavior, while hardware testing was still necessary to find wiring and power problems. This showed that AI was helpful for organizing and checking the design, but its output needed to be compared carefully against the datasheets, lab specifications, and assembled circuit.

title: Lab 2: Multiplexed Seven-Segment Display
text:
Conclusion
The FPGA successfully multiplexed two hexadecimal digits and scanned the 4 × 4 keypad. Total time: 15 hours.
